description: US sanctions the Chinese military's procurement department for buying Russian Su-35 jets and S-400 missiles: the first secondary sanctions on a Chinese entity under a Russia law
Pompeo: waivers for buying Iranian oil end (China's on 2 May); imports "going to zero"
US sanctions Zhuhai Zhenrong, a Chinese state oil trader, for buying Iranian crude after the waivers ended
Hong Kong Autonomy Act signed, allowing secondary sanctions on foreign banks that deal with sanctioned officials, plus an executive order on Hong Kong (unverified)
First sanctions under that Hong Kong order: 11 officials, including Carrie Lam
State Department's report under the Act on 10 officials; starts the clock for sanctions on banks dealing with them (no banks named)
Executive order banning US investment in securities of Chinese military companies from January 2021 (unverified)
Pentagon adds 4 companies to its military-company list, including CNOOC and SMIC. CNOOC is in our sample through the ownership links
Pentagon adds 9 companies, including Xiaomi and COMAC
Biden's order replaces the November 2020 one; Treasury publishes a new list of banned Chinese military companies (unverified)
Biden–Xi call: Biden warns of "implications and consequences" if China materially supports Russia
Executive order 14114: the US may sanction foreign banks for transactions with Russia's military-industrial base

Yellen in China: banks that help channel military or dual-use goods to Russia "expose themselves to the risk of U.S. sanctions" (first signalled on Saturday 6 April, so it counts on Monday's trading day)
Blinken in Beijing: "if China does not address this problem, we will". The WSJ had reported draft sanctions on Chinese banks on 23 April

Treasury redefines Russia's military-industrial base to include everyone blocked under the Russia programme. This sharply widens foreign banks' exposure. Large package, including Chinese and Hong Kong suppliers
Annual Pentagon list of Chinese military companies; adds Tencent
US Russia package calling China the "largest supplier of dual use items"; widens mandatory secondary sanctions; warning to foreign banks
First US sanctions on a Chinese "teapot" refinery buying Iranian oil, and on a China-based crude terminal
EU 18th Russia package: the EU's first measures against Chinese banks (two small border banks)
Treasury Secretary Bessent: two Chinese banks received Treasury letters warning of secondary sanctions over Iranian oil. The same day, Treasury warned financial institutions generally
Annual Pentagon list update; adds Baidu
"Economic Outcast" Iran campaign; foreign banks warned. Bessent on Chinese banks: "no one is above the reach of US sanctions"
